newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares close firmer with help from Dow.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares close firmer with help from Dow.

text.p: Italian shares closed firmer on Friday with support coming from a higher Dow Jones and the slightly firmer trend to domestic bonds, with investors still prepared to buy on any weakness in the market, dealers said.

They added that the market had recovered from its bout of weakness on Thursday, but it lack real conviction today with many stocks slipping back. But the financial sector saw renewed interest with banking group Ambroveneto up 1.17 percent at 9,160 lire and insurer Generali 1.21 percent higher at 38,550 lire.
The all-share Mibtel index ended up 0.58 percent at 15,094 and the blue chip Mib30 0.78 percent higher at 23,008.

Other blue chip stocks such as oil giant ENI, Fiat and Pirelli followed the higher trend, but others such as Olivetti and Edison slipped back, with sellers emerging to push Olivetti down 5.39 percent to 650 lire.
Edison continued to suffer from electricity utility ENEL's decision to halt buying excess electricity from private suppliers. Its shares were off 4.65 percent at 8,257 lire.

Shares in banking group Credito Bergamasco remained suspended after Thursday's halt to trading, pending the release of a statement on the bank's future, which is majority owned by French state-controlled bank Credit Lyonnais.
The French bank is expected to announce its decision to sell its 56.8 percent stake in Credito Bergamasco to another Italian bank Banca Popolare di Verona, dealers said.
